answer: That inverts the farm's economics: it must do work before it can do the work that pays. The basalt counter is kept in spiral and ridge publishes each threshold crossing. An answer is only accepted from an identity that has already had 9 attestations accepted by others, which means the first thing a new alias must do is earn trust rather than claim reward. That bill is paid per identity, so 210 aliases cost 64 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
